text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- International Monetary Fund (IMF) says in a confidential report made available to the newspaper that Portugal will have to cut civil service jobs in order to cut the budget deficit to three percent of Gross Domestic Product in time to qualify to join a single European currency by the end of the century.
- Brazilian group Tavares de Almeida Participacoes, which holds 100 percent of Banco Luso Brasileiro, is studying the possibility of opening a bank in Portugal at the end of 1997.
- Year-on-year growth of 17.7 percent seen in construction and public works in 1996, according to National Association of Public Works Contractors.
- The commission studying the privatisation of airport company ANA may deliver its conclusions to Planning Minister Joao Cravinho today.
- Construction company Soares da Costa won a public competition to build the Macau Culture Centre for 12 billion escudos.
- Silva Correia, former chairman of electricity company EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, is optimistic about success of privatisation of EDP next year.
